run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T10:51:16Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by a chain that starts at the cart service losing its Redis/Valkey storage. frontend-proxy's own ingress spans carried 961.3 error-status spans in the 75-minute window ending 11:06:16 (vs 16,215.8 unset), sampling as error=true with http.status_code 504 and duration of exactly ~15s, while the matching 'router frontend egress' spans ended with http.status_code 0 - the shape of the Envoy upstream timeout. In the same traces the frontend took 501s on GET /api/cart and returned HTTP 500 because cart's gRPC call returned code 9 FAILED_PRECONDITION 'Can't access cart storage. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis'. cart's own logs print 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' repeatedly from 10:51:35 onward, cart's span throughput collapsed from ~14.6/s to ~0.1/s, its Redis child spans (HGET/HMSET/EXPIRE) went to zero, and cart was throttled on CPU at 82-96% of CFS periods against a 45m limit. The dependency valkey-cart stayed Running and Ready with 0 restarts and no OOMKill (working set ~4.3MB under a 10Mi limit), but the redis_* series that otel-collector's redisreceiver scrapes from it froze at ~10:51 and stopped producing samples around 10:54-10:56, while the collector kept exporting all other metrics - evidence that valkey-cart itself stopped answering, not that it crashed. Why valkey-cart stalled is not resolved; valkey's very small container limits (cpu 10m, memory 10Mi) and its rising CFS throttling (up to ~9.8%) are the leading but unproven mechanism, and cart-side CPU starvation is an alternative explanation for the same 'cannot connect' message. Impact is confined to cart and its callers: frontend, checkout and the synthetic load-generator show their own error spans, while product-catalog, ad, recommendation and image-provider on the same node kept normal latency and no error series.

claims.text: frontend-proxy produced 961.29 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans on operation 'ingress' during the 75-minute window ending 11:06:16, against 16,215.84 STATUS_CODE_UNSET 'ingress' spans; its 'router frontend egress' operation contributed 0 error spans, so the error status is recorded on the inbound side only.
The frontend-proxy error rate (5m rate of error-status spans) was 0.0037-0.011/s before 10:51, rose from 0.178/s at 10:51 to a peak of 1.515/s at 10:55, and returned to 0 at 11:04.

Sampled frontend-proxy error spans are operation 'ingress' with status tags error=true, http.status_code=504, otel.status_code=ERROR and duration_us of about 15,000,000 (15s); their child 'router frontend egress' spans carry error="true" and http.status_code="0", indicating the upstream never answered within the proxy timeout.

One complete traced request (trace a545ba7815ee3f559a6bbcc06809bf79 / 89d64c7b2d5cbc297f9fe9426df46e75) shows the edge: load-generator GET 504 at 15.0s -> frontend-proxy ingress 504 at 15.0s -> frontend-proxy egress error http.status_code 0 -> frontend GET span; in the same trace frontend's 'GET /api/cart' ran 501.2s and ended HTTP 500, and its child cart server span 'POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart' ran 479.7s and ended with Status(StatusCode="FailedPrecondition", Detail="Can't access cart storage. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis ... EnsureRedisConnected()").

cart's own server spans errored in the window: 'POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem' 45.23 ERROR and 'POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart' 38.77 ERROR, alongside 2,194.19 and 4,061.84 unset spans respectively; its Redis child operations HGET/HMSET/EXPIRE show only unset status during normal operation.

cart container logs (pod cart-755465879b-t9mf7) show normal AddItemAsync/GetCartAsync lines until about 10:51:33 and then repeated 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' plus 'Error status code ... raised' lines from 10:51:35 through 10:57:52.

cart's overall span rate fell from ~14.6/s (10:35-10:51) to 5.24/s at 10:53, 0.075/s at 10:55 and stayed at 0.065-0.17/s through 11:03; its Redis child span rates HGET ~4.4/s, HMSET/EXPIRE ~2.1/s dropped to exactly 0 from 10:55 onward.

cart's container was already throttled 17-24% of CFS periods before the incident (10:25-10:51) and rose to 34% at 10:53, 76.9-82.8% at 10:55-10:57 and 96.4% at 11:03; its CPU usage rose from ~0.0092 to a peak of 0.0283 cores against a 45m limit.

At 10:57 cart was the most CPU-throttled pod in otel-demo at 82.8%, compared with postgresql 39.3%, frontend 9.5%, product-catalog 9.2%, valkey-cart 6.0%, otel-collector 4.2% and frontend-proxy 0.26%.

The cart deployment sets container limits cpu 45m / memory 165Mi (requests 15m/55Mi) and env VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379; the valkey-cart deployment sets limits cpu 10m / memory 10Mi (requests 2m/4Mi) on image valkey/valkey:8.1.3-alpine - an order of magnitude below the other services' limits.

Pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr was Running and Ready with restartCount 0, an empty lastState (no OOMKilled/terminated history) and container running since 10:18:13; its maximum working set over the window was 4,284,416 bytes against a 10Mi limit, and its CPU usage stayed between ~0.0021 and ~0.0035 cores with CFS throttling rising from ~0.9-3.4% to 5.3-9.8% at 10:55-11:03.

The redis_* series produced by otel-collector's redisreceiver for valkey-cart (job otel-collector, instance 100.96.1.218:8889) behaved normally until ~10:51: redis_memory_used_bytes grew 1,436,536 -> 1,710,360 bytes up to 10:51 and then stayed at exactly 1,710,360, and count_over_time(redis_memory_used_bytes[3m]) fell from a steady 6 samples to 4 at 10:55 and 2 at 10:56, after which no data was returned through 11:07:35.

frontend recorded its own error spans on the cart path: 'executing api route (pages) /api/cart' 79.34 ERROR, 'POST /api/cart' 46.31 ERROR, 'GET /api/cart' 31.53 ERROR, 'POST /api/checkout' 7.12 ERROR, matching error counts on its gRPC client spans 'grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem' (46.31) and 'grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart' (31.53) with rpc.grpc.status_code 9.

checkout recorded 6.75 error spans on its client operation 'oteldemo.CartService/GetCart' and 6.75 on 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' in the window, i.e. its failures are on the cart dependency path.

frontend-proxy span latency degraded with a comparable baseline: the share of its spans under 1s was 0.988 in 10:40-10:45 but 0.701 in 10:52-10:57, while its own container CPU throttling was only 0.26% at 10:57.

Services sharing node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae with cart and valkey-cart did not degrade: product-catalog kept 100% of spans under 1s at both 10:45 and 10:57 and had no error series, ad 0.998->0.996, recommendation 1->1, image-provider 1->1; this does not support node-wide CPU or memory starvation as the cause.

At the time of the Kubernetes queries all 21 otel-demo deployments reported 1 desired / 1 available / 1 ready and all 21 pods were Running with restartCount 0, so no cart or valkey pod was in a crash-loop, Pending or restarted state.

The Service 'valkey-cart' exposes port 6379 with selector opentelemetry.io/name=valkey-cart, and its Endpoints contain the ready address 100.96.2.228 targeting pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-bf4lr, so name resolution and endpoint wiring for cart's VALKEY_ADDR were intact.

A pre-existing cart pod cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s, from ReplicaSet cart-9fd895bb7 that no longer exists (current ReplicaSet cart-755465879b was created 10:18:04), triggered kubelet events 'Stopping container cart' last at 10:54:06Z and Warning FailedKillPod 'error killing pod: failed to KillContainer ... DeadlineExceeded' last at 10:54:05Z, and its container cgroup still reported a steady ~0.0063-0.0068 cores of CPU use with 0 throttled periods across the window.

The lingering terminating pod cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s (FailedKillPod DeadlineExceeded at 10:54) is rejected as the cause of the alert: its CPU use was flat at ~6.5 millicores before and during the 10:51 onset with zero throttled periods, it is not an endpoint of the cart Service, and no evidence ties it to valkey-cart's loss of responsiveness.

Primary explanation: the cart service lost its Redis/Valkey storage because valkey-cart itself stopped serving requests around 10:51-10:55 (its own redisreceiver-exported series froze and then stopped while the collector kept exporting everything else), so cart's redis connects failed with 'Wasn't able to connect to redis', cart requests hung for 450-500s, frontend returned HTTP 500 on /api/cart, and frontend-proxy hit its 15s upstream timeout and emitted the 504 error spans that trigger RequestErrorRate.

Mechanism candidate 1 for valkey-cart's stall: its container is limited to cpu 10m and memory 10Mi and its CFS throttling ratio doubled to 5.3-9.8% during the incident, which could stall its event loop long enough that clients' handshakes and INFO scrapes time out; this is only partially supported because its average CPU use (~0.0035 cores) stayed well below the 0.01 core limit and memory (~4.3MB) well below 10Mi.

Mechanism candidate 2: cart's own 45m CPU limit and 82-96% CFS throttling starved the .NET process so that redis connects and continuations timed out client-side, making valkey look unreachable; this is counter-indicated by the independent stop of valkey's own redis_* series but is not excluded, and cart's CPU rise may be an effect of the hung-request backlog rather than the trigger.

Raise and review the container limits of cart (cpu 45m) and especially valkey-cart (cpu 10m / memory 10Mi), which are far below the other otel-demo services, then confirm valkey responsiveness with a direct PING/latency probe; verify whether these values were introduced by the 10:18:04 rollout that created ReplicaSets cart-755465879b and valkey-cart-58df56c79c.

Follow up on the kubelet's FailedKillPod DeadlineExceeded warnings for cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s (last at 10:54:05Z) and on the absence of any valkey-cart or otel-collector log lines, since the in-process reason valkey stopped answering cannot be read from the available telemetry.

gaps: change_history is not integrated, so it cannot be determined whether the cart (45m cpu) and valkey-cart (10m cpu / 10Mi memory) limits or other manifests changed in the 10:18:04 rollout that replaced ReplicaSet cart-9fd895bb7 with cart-755465879b.

The valkey-cart container produced zero log lines in the whole authorized window (fetch_pod_logs returned no_data for both current and previous instances), so the reason the valkey process stopped serving commands cannot be read; it cannot be verified whether it was CPU throttling, a blocking command, fork/disk stall or something else.

Prometheus rule lookup for rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no_data, so the alert's exact expression, threshold and evaluation interval could not be verified; the reported 'current: 1.0888888888888888' was not matched to a specific rule.
Instant query of redis_memory_used_bytes at 11:07:00 returned no series, so whether valkey-cart recovered after the authorized window (11:07:35) is unknown.

Node-level CPU and memory metrics are not present in this Prometheus (only node_namespace_pod_container:* series), so pressure on node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae cannot be measured directly; node health was only inferred from unchanged latency of other pods on it.
Secrets cannot be read, so any valkey authentication, maxmemory or persistence configuration on valkey-cart is unverified.
The frontend-proxy error sample shows http.status_code=504 rows, but the exact distribution of error status codes across all 961 error spans is unknown because only a sampled slice was read.
next_steps: Check the alert rule definition and history for RequestErrorRate on frontend-proxy to confirm the expression and the 1.0888 value.
Run redis-cli PING/LATENCY/INFO against valkey-cart:6379 (or exec into the pod) to confirm whether the instance is responsive now and after the window.
Compare cart and valkey-cart deployment manifests and resource limits against the pre-10:18 ReplicaSet revision, using change history when available.
Inspect node i-0146cb0d0caf26bae pressure (CPU, throttling, disk) with node-level monitoring outside this Prometheus.
Review why the kubelet could not kill the cart container in cart-9fd895bb7-kg98s and clear any leftover cgroup/container on that node.
